# The drill format

A drill is one JSON document. The app validates it on arrival and rejects the whole thing if any part
of it is wrong, so it is worth getting right rather than nearly right.

```json
{ "format": "ptb.drill/1", "title": "...", "field": "11-a-side", "phases": [ ... ] }
```

Every drill needs `format`, `title`, `field` and at least one phase.

## Limits

| | |
|---|---|
| `format` | must be exactly `ptb.drill/1` |
| `field` | `11-a-side`, `9-a-side`, `7-a-side`, `futsal` |
| phases | 1 to 19 |
| `caption` | up to 120 characters |
| `say` | up to 400 characters |
| `count` on a player or cone row | up to 12 |

## Phases

Each phase is a complete picture of the board, not a change to the one before. Write out every player
in every phase; anyone left out has left the pitch.

A phase may carry `role` (`setup`, `instruction`, `execution`, `explanation`, `coaching`), `say` (the narration), `caption` and `at`
(`top`, `middle`, `bottom`) for the caption's place on screen, plus `players`, `cones`,
`nets`, `ball` and `arrows`.

**A phase's `say` describes the movement that happens as the board changes *into* the next phase.**
That is the one thing most easily got backwards, and getting it backwards makes the narration
describe what the viewer has already watched.

## Places

Positions are named rather than numeric. `[x, y]` is accepted, where x runs 0 at the left touchline
to 1 at the right, and y runs 0 at the far goal line to 1 at your own - but a name is clearer and
survives a change of pitch.

A drill is always written from the home team's point of view: home defends the bottom, so "own" is
high y and "attacking" is low y.

**Lanes** — `left`, `left-centre`, `centre`, `right-centre`, `right`

**Bands** — `defensive-third`, `middle-third`, `attacking-third`

Combine any lane with any band: `left-attacking-third`, `centre-middle-third`.

**Landmarks** — `own-goal`, `own-six`, `own-box`, `own-penalty-spot`, `top-of-d`, `own-corner-left`, `own-corner-right`, `centre-spot`, `centre-circle`, `halfway-left`, `halfway-right`, `left-touchline`, `right-touchline`, `halfway-line`, `own-goal-line`, `attacking-goal-line`, `left-wing`, `right-wing`, `attacking-top-of-d`, `attacking-penalty-spot`, `attacking-box`, `attacking-six`, `attacking-goal`, `attacking-corner-left`, `attacking-corner-right`

`attacking-box` · `attacking-corner-left` · `attacking-corner-right` · `attacking-goal` · `attacking-goal-line` · `attacking-penalty-spot` · `attacking-six` · `attacking-third` · `attacking-top-of-d` · `centre-attacking-third` · `centre-circle` · `centre-defensive-third` · `centre-middle-third` · `centre-spot` · `defensive-third` · `halfway-left` · `halfway-line` · `halfway-right` · `left-attacking-third` · `left-centre-attacking-third` · `left-centre-defensive-third` · `left-centre-middle-third` · `left-defensive-third` · `left-middle-third` · `left-touchline` · `left-wing` · `middle-third` · `own-box` · `own-corner-left` · `own-corner-right` · `own-goal` · `own-goal-line` · `own-penalty-spot` · `own-six` · `right-attacking-third` · `right-centre-attacking-third` · `right-centre-defensive-third` · `right-centre-middle-third` · `right-defensive-third` · `right-middle-third` · `right-touchline` · `right-wing` · `top-of-d`

## Shirt numbers are not what the board shows

A player is written as a team and a number, but the board draws the away team from
21 up: **an away player's disc reads its number plus 20.**

| written | drawn on the board |
|---|---|
| `{ "team": "home", "number": 9 }` | 9 |
| `{ "team": "away", "number": 4 }` | 24 |
| `{ "team": "away", "number": 1 }` | 21 (the keeper) |

**Narration and captions must use the drawn number**, because that is the only one the viewer can
see. Saying "four closes him down" over a disc reading 24 is simply wrong on
screen.

The same split catches the ball. `carriedBy` and `passTo` take the **written** number, and
`team` defaults to home - so `{ "carriedBy": 4 }` means home 4, never away 4. Give the ball to an
away player with `{ "carriedBy": 4, "team": "away" }`. A ball handed to a player who is not on the
pitch is rejected rather than quietly left where it was.

## Other vocabulary

| | |
|---|---|
| cone colours | `orange`, `yellow`, `blue`, `green`, `red` |
| directions for a row | `up`, `down`, `left`, `right` |
| net `facing` | `0`, `45`, `90`, `135`, `180`, `225`, `270`, `315` |

## Spacing that looks wrong even when it is right

Markers keep a constant size on screen, so they do not shrink with the pitch. At zoom 1 a marker
covers roughly this much grass:

| field | |
|---|---|
| `11-a-side` | player 7.8m, net 7.8m, cone 5.4m |
| `9-a-side` | player 7.8m, net 7.8m, cone 5.4m |
| `7-a-side` | player 7.8m, net 7.8m, cone 5.4m |
| `futsal` | player 2.6m, net 2.6m, cone 1.8m |

Ask for a queue three metres apart on a full pitch and the positions are exact while the discs sit
on top of each other. The answer is to zoom in, not to space things further apart than they are in
real life. Advisory - nothing enforces it.

Two things worth avoiding because they read as mistakes: putting a player on the same spot as a net
(the net draws underneath and disappears), and leaving defenders standing still while attackers move,
which makes any coaching point about them hollow.

`make_qr.py` refuses anything that will not fit rather than truncating it.
